newsitem.title: USA: Stand-alone deal on Chicago airport-Ill. governor.
newsitem.headline: Stand-alone deal on Chicago airport-Ill. governor.

text.p: Illinois Gov. Jim Edgar said Monday that a deal with Chicago Mayor Richard Daley to reopen a small airport on the city's lakefront did not include any other proposals.

Speaking at a press availability in Springfield, Edgar said the compromise to keep Meigs Field open for five years did not include any deals on a domed, multi-use facility in Chicago or other high-profile proposals.

A Chicago newspaper report last month had linked a possible deal over the airport to a domed stadium that would be used by the Chicago Bears football team and by conventions, as well as Daley's help in getting a $610 million state general obligation bond authorization bill passed with Democratic lawmaker support.
Edgar, who has continually proposed the bonding bill, has seen it fail due to the lack of support from Democrats whose votes are needed to garner a required three-fifths vote on the bill.
Edgar and Daley announced the agreement over Meigs Fields at simulateous news conferences in Springfield and Chicago on Monday.

Under the agreement, the city will reopen the airport, used mainly by business and state aircraft, for five years. Following the five years, the city and Chicago Park District would implement their plan to turn the airport into a $27 million, bond-financed nature park.

The deal also calls for the dismissal of state litigation filed to block the park plan. In addition, city and state officials would work to repeal legislation, signed into law Dec. 16 by Edgar, allowing for a state takeover of the airport on June 1.
"This agreement, I believe, is the best agreement that could be reached," Edgar said.
He said the deal was finalized Monday morning, adding that the five years was a compromise between seven years proposed by the state and three years offered by the city.
